stage1.impression: A night quay with a canal, a lamp post, bollards and a flat modern facade of blown-white windows. A coloured-ring glass globe on a black drum sits in the middle and throws a pale, pastel elliptical light pool toward the water. The water reflections are the most photographic part. Everything else reads as CG: a facade of identical blank white rectangles, clean untextured pavers with no wear, an empty dark foreground, a crushed plinth and a dim hero. A jury would see a generic render of a sculpture on a generic quay, not a specific, striking work in Amsterdam.

blocking_9: The globe must be the brightest and most saturated thing in the frame after the practicals: globe region lum_median >= 45, with rims that visibly glow rather than just catch the spot

The coloured shadow must read at a glance as the globe drawn in saturated light: whole, inside the pool, on the paving, clearly brighter than the paving around it, and not cut by a visible cone edge or the kerb
The windows across the canal must stop reading as blank white cards: no clipping, warm, varied in level, with something behind the glass, and fewer of them
The paving and kerb need real stone at 1:1 (worn, uneven, damp in places, a stone kerb edge), and the dead foreground must be cut or filled
The plinth must read as blackened steel with an edge highlight, not a black hole
The far houses must read as Amsterdam (narrow brick gabled canal houses), not a generic flat-fronted block

defects.what: Lit windows are flat pure-white rectangles (p95 242, clip 1.1 %) with no interior, curtains or variation, in a regular grid. Reads as emissive cards
Facade is a plain dark slab with uniform pilasters, no brick, gables or cornices. Not identifiable as Amsterdam
Globe is dim (median 25). The rims read as lit by the spot more than glowing from inside, and the faces read as dark smoked glass, so the hero sits at almost the same level as the background
Plinth is a crushed black cylinder (crush 35 %, median 13) with no steel sheen or edge highlight
The coloured shadow is pastel and weak (median 43 against paving 31). It lies partly behind the globe and is cut by the hard elliptical edge of the 18 degree cone, which reads as a theatre spot
The pool and shadow run into the kerb or water edge and are truncated there
The foreground paving is a large, empty, uniform area (p5 to p95 range only 15) of clean identical pavers with no wear, stains, damp or joint variation. Dead third of the frame
Bollards are identical copies at regular spacing, and the quay edge has no stone kerb detail
A single small lamp post makes almost no pool of light on the paving. The left side has no source to explain its light
The blue-violet sky and haze band in the top left is the only cool area. Acceptable, but the haze reads as a flat fog wall at the horizon

changes.problem: The hero globe is too dim to lead the frame. Its rims do not glow, so it reads as a dark glass object rather than a light artwork.

evidence.measured: lum_median 25.0, p95 134. Faces dark. Same median as the facade behind (26.8)

change.setting: the globe: the rims' glow (emission strength)

changes.expected: Six saturated coloured rims glowing clearly, with light spilling a little into the clear faces. Globe region median about 45 to 60 while the faces stay clear.

changes.problem: The coloured shadow, the purpose of the frame, is pastel, half hidden behind the globe, cut by the cone's hard elliptical edge and truncated at the kerb.

evidence.measured: lum_median 43.2 against paving 31. The cone edge is visible as a sharp ellipse. The shadow runs to the kerb at around x 740 to 860, y 380 to 470

change.setting: the hard spot: power, cone, position
change.to: 1800 W, cone 30 deg with a soft 15 % blend, from [-3.5, -8.0, 8.5] at [0.4, -2.2, 0.0], so that the shadow falls fully on the paving between the plinth and the kerb and the pool's edge lies outside the globe's shadow

changes.expected: One complete, saturated coloured shadow of the globe (six coloured bands, crisp rim lines) lying on the paving toward the water, inside a soft-edged pool. Shadow area median 70 or more, and no visible cone ellipse cutting the shadow.

changes.problem: The windows across the canal are clipped white cards that pull the eye from the hero and give the scene away as CG.

evidence.measured: p95 241.8, clip_pct 1.11. Uniform flat white with no interior

change.setting: the houses across: windows lit and their glow
change.to: 0.2 lit, glow 0.25 with plus or minus 50 % random variation per window, 2700 K, and an interior card or curtain texture behind the glass

changes.expected: A scattering of warm amber windows at different levels, readable through the glass, none clipped. Their reflections in the canal stay as the strong secondary element.

changes.problem: The paving is clean, uniform and textureless, so the foreground reads as a game floor.

evidence.measured: lum_p5 24.5, lum_p95 39.5, range 15.1. Identical pavers at 1:1

change.setting: the paving and the stone kerb: materials' finish
change.to: worn clinker pavers with per-brick tone variation of plus or minus 15 %, dirt in the joints, damp patches with roughness 0.15 to 0.35 that catch the lamp and the window reflections, and a 300 mm granite kerb with a chipped edge at the water

changes.expected: Paving with visible tonal variety and small specular glints from the windows and the lamp. Foreground range doubles.

changes.problem: The bottom third is empty, and the globe and shadow are small in the frame.

evidence.measured: About 31 % of the frame is uniform paving with nothing in it

change.to: position [3.8, -8.4, 2.8], at [0.2, -2.4, 0.5], 35 mm, so that the plinth's base sits near the lower third and the whole shadow lies between the globe and the kerb in frame

changes.expected: The globe and its shadow fill the middle of the frame and the foreground is cut to about a fifth. Still seen from a little above, as the card asks.

changes.problem: The plinth reads as a crushed black void, not blackened steel.

change.setting: the plinth: materials' finish (allowed as finish only, shape fixed)
change.to: blackened steel: base colour about #1c1916, metallic 1, roughness 0.35 to 0.55 varied, slight brown patina, so the spot and the globe's rims leave a soft sheen and a crisp top edge highlight

changes.expected: The drum reads as metal with a lit top edge and coloured reflections from the rims.

changes.problem: The quay is empty and its bollards repeat, so there is no sign of a real, lived-in place.

evidence.measured: Five identical bollards at even spacing. No bicycle, bench or person

change.to: vary the bollards' height and wear (Amsterdammertjes, rust-red with scuffs, spacing varied), add one parked Dutch bicycle against a lamp post at left, a bench in the lamp's pool, and two far-off figures on the far quay or the bridge

changes.expected: The frame reads as a real Amsterdam quay at festival time, with scale cues next to the 2 m globe.

changes.problem: The street lamp gives almost no pool of light, so the left half's light has no source and the 'room's own light' is incoherent.

evidence.measured: lum_median 38.4 with no visible pool under the lamp at x 160 to 210

change.to: 2 x point 120 W, 2200 K, inside a frosted lantern so the lamp head glows without clipping, and a second lamp at right on the near quay

changes.expected: Warm, falling-off pools under the lamps on wet-looking paving. A coherent set of practicals with the globe's coloured pool as the odd one out.

out_of_scope.request: Replace the flat modern facade with narrow brick gabled Amsterdam canal houses (stepped and bell gables, hoist beams, tall sash windows)
out_of_scope.why: The card allows the houses' brick finish but not their form. This is a site and asset decision for the owner, and it is the biggest single reason the place reads as generic rather than Amsterdam.

out_of_scope.request: Make the shadow's colours more saturated by deepening the discs' tint
out_of_scope.why: The discs' colours and the clear faces are fixed. Saturation must come from the spot's power and from exposure only.

out_of_scope.request: The brief's interiors and listening-bar criteria (concrete, timber, cozy room)
out_of_scope.why: This frame is an outdoor festival light artwork on a quay, so the room criteria were applied as night-exterior photo criteria.
